messages:
sre-bot: [ALERT] 4623456789 - High rate of CUDA_ILLEGAL_MEMORY_ACCESS on serving-runtime in us-west-2. 48 unique pods reporting OOM/CUDA errors in last 3m. auto-evacuate policy triggered.

sre-bot: affected service: gpu-serving, impact: increased 5xx, node-flap risk. incident-id=inc-20260315-01

maria (oncall): acknowledging. I'm oncall for infra today, pulling logs.

kevin (eng-runtime): thanks — I'm joining. early guess: recent pagewalk codepath + continuous batching might trigger misaligned deviceaddr when eviction happens. Could be race during KV cache eviction.

liam (ops): seeing nodes with repeated kernel oops in dmesg: "NVIDIA: illegal device address at 0x7f8b1a2c0000" then container crashes. sample from node gpu-node-12: ```
Mar 15 18:24:11 gpu-node-12 kernel: panic: gpu pagewalk: misaligned deviceaddr
Mar 15 18:24:11 gpu-node-12 nvidia: gpu0: Illegal memory access at 0x7f8b1a2c0000
Backtrace: gpu_pagewalk+0x3f /opt/runtime/kernel/pagewalk.c:412
```

maria (oncall): copying pod logs for pod gpu-serving-abc-xyz: ```
I0323 18:23:59.123 ServingRuntime: request id=abc123 token=...
ERROR cuda: illegal memory access during attention_kv_write (kv_cache.cpp:88)
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what(): cudaErrorIllegalAddress: misaligned device address
```

kevin (eng-runtime): that stacktrace lines up with a race we instrumented before. Not the same as earlier pagewalk incidents — this one shows misaligned pointer inside our KV write path. Could be a concurrent eviction while write is in-flight.

cs-ops: getting customer reports — tenant "finly" seeing 40% 502s in us-west-2 since 18:22. They called CS and asked for ETA.

maria (oncall): immediate mitigation: 1) cordon and drain the most-affected GPU nodes, 2) enable cpu-fallback routing for high-priority tenants, 3) spin up standby Dedicated CPU pool and route traffic. executing now.

liam (ops): running drain on gpu-node-12 and gpu-node-15: ```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-12 && kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -l app=gpu-serving
```
output: node/gpu-node-12 cordoned
pod gpu-serving-abc-xyz evicted, restarted on gpu-node-21 (fallback)

devops: increased ai-fallback replica count from 4 -> 12, updated routing rule in edge: route policy weight for model_variant=cpu-quantized -> 0.35 for tenant finly.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-9984 created, severity P1. Oncall: maria (oncall).

kevin (eng-runtime): while we evacuate, let's add a conservative lock around KV-cache eviction on canary nodes to avoid concurrent write/evict. I'll prepare a hotpatch build with semaphore guard and limited change set. canary image: redwood/serving:hotfix-misaligned-20260315.

maria (oncall): approved. kevin, roll to 2 canary nodes in us-west-2 first, then monitor. liam, keep draining remaining noisy nodes. devops, keep CPU fallback active. cs-ops, send interim update to finly: we have mitigations in place and a targeted hotfix; ETA ~30-45m for canary verification.

kevin (eng-runtime): pushing canary now. kubectl set image deployment/serving-canary serving=redwood/serving:hotfix-misaligned-20260315 -n gpu-prod-usw2

kevin (eng-runtime): canary pods started, healthchecks passing: ```
Liveness: OK
Startup: OK
Errors/CUDA_ILLEGAL_MEMORY_ACCESS: 0 (in last 60s)
```

maria (oncall): observing error rate drop on canary region. overall 5xx rate down from 12% -> 6% since cpu-fallback + canary. still seeing some node reboots unrelated to canary.

liam (ops): I've isolated 6 nodes with repeated NVidia firmware warnings that correlate with our busy eviction windows. Taking them out of rotation and filing hardware ticket.

cs-ops: updated customer finly via status page: "We are mitigating a GPU runtime issue impacting inference in us-west-2. Traffic is being routed to CPU fallback and a canary hotfix is rolling out. We expect partial recovery in ~45 min. Sorry for the disruption."

kevin (eng-runtime): after 20m canary stable, initiating staged rollout: 10% -> 30% -> 60% with 5m observation windows. If any CUDA_ILLEGAL_MEMORY_ACCESS, auto-rollback.

sre-bot: auto-rollout policy is enabled for hotfix-misaligned-20260315. Watcher alerts set.

maria (oncall): quick postmortem actions (todo):  - capture full dmesg and kernel oops from affected nodes,  - add regression test for eviction during concurrent writes,  - add more tracing around KV cache lock acquisition,  - coordinate with driver/firmware team on NVidia warnings.

kevin (eng-runtime): agreed. I'll open PR for semaphore guard + unit/regression test and link to PD-9984.

liam (ops): hardware ticket created HT-5732 for firmware/board checks. nodes quarantined: gpu-node-{12,15,23,47,58,61}.

cs-ops: finly acknowledged the update, asked for root cause followup. I'll schedule post-incident call if root cause needs long-term mitigation.

maria (oncall): closing immediate customer-impact window once rollout reaches 100% and 5xxs under 1%. we'll keep incident open for RCA until tomorrow. handing off to kevin for code fix and to liam for infra followup. next handoff timestamp: 4623457050.

kevin (eng-runtime): taking lead for RCA and fix. will update PD-9984 and link to a follow-up doc.

liam (ops): taking infra/action items and hw followups.

sre-bot: Incident PD-9984 status: mitigated -> partial-recovery. Keep monitoring.

maria (oncall): thanks team. I'm leaving the incident in progress; kevin and liam will continue the investigation and postmortem. ping me for any escalations. :white_check_mark:
